title: The Trend-to-Video Newsroom
pitch: Agent-Reach gives an agent free, API-fee-free eyes on Twitter, Reddit, YouTube and more, but it only hands back raw findings — someone still has to turn 'here's what's trending' into something watchable. OpenMontage can turn a text brief into a fully produced video, but it needs a human to supply the brief and the angle every time. Chain them: every morning, an agent uses Agent-Reach to pull the top 3 debates or stories in a niche (say, fitness gear, or indie hacking), drafts a 60-second script and talking points from what it found, and hands that straight to OpenMontage to produce a narrated, captioned short. The output is a same-day 'here's what people are saying about X' video channel that costs a few dollars in compute and zero hours of a human's time, sellable as a white-label daily-digest video feed to niche newsletters, subreddits-turned-brands, or small media accounts that want a video presence but have no video team.
why_now: Both repos trended on the same day with complementary gaps — Agent-Reach solves the 'agents can't read the live internet' problem, OpenMontage solves the 'agents can't produce finished video' problem — and short-form video news/recap accounts are exactly the format small creators are racing to fill right now.
